wearable-firmware.title: nRF52 wearable firmware
wearable-firmware.focus: Firmware and host tools for multichannel acquisition, wearable sensor integration, and BLE data streaming.
flow: Sensor interfaces
ADS131M04/M02 ADCs, MAX30208 temperature sensing, BNO080 inertial sensing, and MAX20303 power management form the documented integration context.
Acquisition & RTOS
Interrupt-driven acquisition coordinates sampling with firmware threads. Timing, sample identity, and bounded buffering make the producer/consumer boundary observable.
BLE transport
Device identity, battery telemetry, and GATT streaming connect the wearable to host software. In the lab below, MTU and connection interval control an approximate payload budget.
Python host
Bleak handles connectivity; PySide6 and pyqtgraph support discovery, live visualization, battery monitoring, and CSV recording.
decisions: Acquisition timing
A consistent sampling schedule must remain understandable when wireless delivery slows.
Inspect interrupt cadence and sequence counters independently from host arrival times.
Transport backpressure
A faster producer cannot be solved by an unbounded queue.
Measure payload size, connection capacity, queue depth, and the selected overflow policy.
Board observability
Signal, timing, power, and decoding faults can look similar at the plot.
Use a scope or logic analyzer at the interface, then compare raw words and decoded host data.
try: Run at 250 Hz with 2 channels. Disconnect BLE: sampling continues while the queue fills.
Set MTU to 23 and sample rate to 1000 Hz. Inspect capacity, latency, and overflow.
Restore MTU to 247 and reconnect. Watch the queue drain if transport capacity exceeds production.
wearable-firmware.assumption: Application-payload budget model. It omits BLE airtime, retransmissions, radio coexistence, and measured hardware performance. Overflow drops the newest frame. The plotted waveform is synthetic and display-decimated.
wearable-firmware.alt: OBSL multimodal armband design and physical wearable prototype
wearable-firmware.context: Texas A&M University · Current research engineering
wearable-firmware.credit: OBSL lab-platform photo, Texas A&M University. The interactive trace is synthetic.

documented.title: Problem
paragraphs: A wearable data path has to connect sensor acquisition, device firmware, wireless delivery, and host-side inspection. I developed the C/C++ firmware and Python tools that connect those boundaries at Texas A&M’s Optical Bio-Sensing Laboratory.

documented.title: Constraint
paragraphs: Sampling and BLE delivery run on different schedules. A live plot alone cannot identify whether a problem begins at the sensor, the bus transaction, firmware timing, or host decoding. The system also needs device identification, battery telemetry, and useful access during board bring-up.

documented.title: Decision
paragraphs: I implemented interrupt-driven multichannel acquisition in Zephyr and BLE GATT streaming on nRF52840 / nRF52832 targets. I integrated ADC, temperature, inertial, and power-management devices over SPI, I2C, and GPIO. This keeps acquisition and the host communication path explicit rather than treating the plotted signal as the whole system.

documented.title: Result
paragraphs: I built a device-to-host workflow with BLE discovery, device selection, live plots, battery monitoring, CSV logging, and automated collection. I used PySide6, pyqtgraph, and Bleak for the host tools. My contribution covered firmware, sensor integration, custom-board bring-up, and the software used to inspect acquired data.

lucid-powertrain.title: EV powertrain platform software
lucid-powertrain.focus: Platform drivers, middleware, AUTOSAR integration, on-chip debugging, and automated bench validation at Lucid.
flow: Platform drivers
Documented work covers low-level drivers and middleware for powertrain ECUs, alongside hardware/software integration and debugging.
AUTOSAR integration
BSW, RTE, and MCAL layers provide the documented software-integration context. The diagram summarizes responsibilities rather than exposing a proprietary architecture.
ECU bring-up & debug
On-chip inspection, defect triage, code review, and repeatable bench conditions connect an isolated software module to behavior on the target.
Automated validation
Python and Shell scripts support validation workflows. The interactive model isolates freshness and fault recovery as a public teaching example.
decisions: Command freshness
A new demand value is useful only if a valid message reaches the consumer in time.
Track the age of the last valid frame and a defined timeout threshold.
Fault containment
Communication loss must produce an explicit state transition.
Observe a safe/inhibit output, record the reason, and test recovery conditions.
Reproducibility
An intermittent integration defect needs a repeatable trigger and useful evidence.
Log sequence, time, validity, state transitions, and the condition used to reproduce the problem.
try: Run the bench, change demand, then pause CAN delivery. Watch the freshness watchdog trip.
Restore delivery. Three valid frames are required to re-arm this example.
Increase bus load or corrupt frames. Export the trace and inspect the state transitions.
lucid-powertrain.assumption: Generic communication and watchdog teaching model, not Lucid production logic. Delay is an illustrative bus-load model. Recovery requires three valid frames; no real vehicle or ECU is connected.
lucid-powertrain.alt: Powertrain software workflow: C/C++ platform drivers, AUTOSAR integration, ECU bring-up and debugging, and Python/Shell bench validation with a feedback loop
lucid-powertrain.context: Lucid · Embedded Software Engineer · Jan 2024 – Apr 2026
lucid-powertrain.credit: Original generic software diagram and browser simulation; no vehicle photo, production ECU logic, or confidential implementation.

documented.title: Problem
paragraphs: Powertrain ECU software depends on low-level drivers, middleware, and application integration working together on the target. At Lucid, I developed and debugged platform software at that hardware–software boundary.

documented.title: Constraint
paragraphs: The work ran within automotive development and validation processes. A module working in isolation does not establish correct behavior after its hardware interfaces, platform dependencies, and application interactions are integrated.

documented.title: Decision
paragraphs: I developed low-level drivers and middleware and worked across AUTOSAR BSW, RTE, and MCAL integration. I used on-chip debugging to investigate hardware/software integration issues and reviewed real-time code for responsiveness.

documented.title: Result
paragraphs: I contributed integrated ECU platform software and repeatable bench-validation workflows. I wrote Python and Shell automation for validation and supported code review, defect triage, and software integration. My full-time role ran January 2024–April 2026, following an August–December 2023 internship.

cardiovascular-phantom.title: Cardiovascular phantom acquisition
cardiovascular-phantom.focus: Firmware and Python acquisition tools for pressure-monitoring experiments on physical physiological phantom platforms.
flow: Physical test platform
Anatomical fixtures and pulsatile flow provide repeatable research conditions. The lab photographs show the wider team platform and devices under test.
Electrical interface
Analog/digital pressure sensing, ADC/DAC interfaces, and level shifting connect the experiment to the Portenta H7 acquisition system.
Firmware acquisition
Conversion, sample timing, and channel alignment determine what the firmware makes observable to the host.
Host verification
Python acquisition and plotting, scopes, and logic analyzers support waveform inspection and root-cause debugging.
decisions: Range and resolution
A pressure range maps into a finite converter code space.
Compare full-scale range, ADC resolution, and the reconstructed signal.
Temporal detail
A low sample rate may hide waveform shape even when the pulse is still visible.
Compare sampled and reference traces while changing acquisition rate.
Channel alignment
Different channels may not represent the same instant.
Inspect timestamping and relative delay before interpreting channel differences.
try: Run at 100 Hz and 12 bits, then reduce sampling to 10 Hz. Compare waveform shape.
Change ADC resolution from 8 to 16 bits and inspect the pressure-per-code value.
Add noise and channel delay; export the sampled data for inspection.
cardiovascular-phantom.assumption: Synthetic Gaussian pulse shape with a secondary feature, not a physiological or diagnostic model. Converter range is fixed to 0–250 mmHg for illustration. Noise and delay are controlled examples, not measured platform specifications.
cardiovascular-phantom.alt: OBSL human arm phantom with wearable devices mounted on a test fixture
cardiovascular-phantom.context: Texas A&M University · Biomedical test systems
cardiovascular-phantom.credit: OBSL lab-platform photo, Texas A&M University.

documented.title: Problem
paragraphs: Biomedical test setups need firmware and host software that make pressure signals inspectable during experiments. I supported Portenta H7 pressure-monitoring work at Texas A&M’s Optical Bio-Sensing Laboratory.

documented.title: Constraint
paragraphs: ADC / DAC integration, voltage-domain interfaces, and waveform behavior must agree before a host plot can be interpreted. A physical phantom also needs repeatable bench conditions rather than a display that merely resembles a physiological waveform.

documented.title: Decision
paragraphs: I integrated the Portenta H7 acquisition path, supported level shifting, and verified waveforms with bench tools. I developed Python test software to inspect the pressure-monitoring experiments and their device interfaces.

documented.title: Result
paragraphs: My work connected pressure acquisition, ADC / DAC interfaces, waveform verification, and host-side testing. I contributed embedded integration and test software used to investigate the bench signal path.

yocto-patient-monitoring.title: Yocto Linux patient-monitoring project
yocto-patient-monitoring.eyebrow: EMBEDDED LINUX / SENSORS / MQTT / CLOUD PATH
yocto-patient-monitoring.focus: A BeagleBone Black project integrating MAX30100 and LM35 sensing with a Yocto Linux platform and MQTT-based cloud communication.
flow: Sensor inputs
MAX30100 and LM35 are the documented sensing components. Acquisition and network delivery are separate interfaces to reason about.
Yocto Linux target
The BeagleBone Black target supplies the embedded Linux environment. Image configuration, sensor availability, timestamps, and application state are useful verification boundaries.
MQTT client & outbox
Serialization and connectivity turn a local sample into a message. Buffering and retry behavior should be explicit rather than hidden in a counter.
Broker & consumer
The documented project includes MQTT cloud communication. The browser model adds a visible outbox, ACK behavior, and subscriber deduplication as an educational exploration.
decisions: Offline policy
Best-effort delivery and an acknowledged outbox behave differently during outages.
Compare QoS 0 loss with the demo QoS 1 queue and retry policy.
Duplicate delivery
A lost acknowledgment can cause a message to be sent again.
Keep a stable message ID across retries and inspect subscriber deduplication.
Bounded storage
An offline target has finite memory.
Set an outbox limit, expose drops, and inspect what happens after reconnecting.
try: Select QoS 1, disconnect MQTT, generate samples, then reconnect.
Drop acknowledgments while connected. Retries reuse the same message ID.
Switch to QoS 0 during an outage and compare loss with the queued mode.
yocto-patient-monitoring.assumption: Illustrative MQTT application model, not a broker or full MQTT protocol implementation. QoS 1 retries until acknowledged; the subscriber deduplicates IDs. No real patient information, cloud credentials, or external connection is used.
yocto-patient-monitoring.alt: Sensor inputs, Yocto Linux on BeagleBone, MQTT communication, and a remote monitoring consumer
yocto-patient-monitoring.credit: Original explanatory system diagram based on the resume project.

documented.title: Problem
paragraphs: I developed a patient-monitoring project that joined sensor acquisition on a BeagleBone Black with MQTT-based cloud communication. The work ran July–September 2023.

documented.title: Constraint
paragraphs: An embedded Linux sensing path crosses several boundaries: the target image, device interfaces, sensor reads, and delivery to a remote consumer. A successful message alone does not establish correct sensor values or a reproducible target configuration.

documented.title: Decision
paragraphs: I used Yocto Linux on the BeagleBone Black and integrated MAX30100 and LM35 sensors. I connected the acquired data to an MQTT communication path so that acquisition and remote delivery could be considered separately.

documented.title: Result
paragraphs: I built an embedded Linux monitoring system with sensor integration and cloud messaging. My documented contribution is the target sensing and MQTT communication path.

mips-fifo-digital-design.title: MIPS processor & FIFO digital design
mips-fifo-digital-design.focus: A 32-bit MIPS processor project and separate synchronous/asynchronous FIFO designs, developed with Quartus Prime and ModelSim.
flow: RTL description
The documented projects are a single-cycle MIPS processor in VHDL and separate 8 × 8 FIFO designs in Verilog.
Stimulus & control
Instruction operands, memory operations, and queue read/write conditions provide controlled stimulus for reasoning about logic.
Simulation & checks
Quartus Prime and ModelSim form the documented design/verification workflow. Ordering and boundary flags matter as much as a successful nominal transfer.
Inspection
The architecture reference comes from the published article. The browser lab exposes architectural state; it is not an exported RTL simulation.
decisions: Instruction state
The destination register must receive the intended result at write-back.
Follow fetch, decode, execute, memory, and write-back without conflating an animation with a clock-accurate design.
Memory boundaries
A word access must have a valid aligned address in the model.
Inspect address calculation, memory read/write, and rejected out-of-range operations.
FIFO boundaries
Full and empty conditions are explicit control states.
Exercise wrap-around, rejected writes/reads, almost-full/empty flags, and pointer representations.
try: Step through the Memory program stage by stage; inspect SW, LW, and register write-back.
Run the Branch program and follow the program counter as the loop exits.
Open FIFO, set producer faster than consumer, and inspect overflow rejection and pointer wrap.
mips-fifo-digital-design.assumption: Instruction-level teaching subset: 32 registers, 16 memory words, unsigned wrapping arithmetic, and no branch delay slots. FIFO clocks are independent software timers, not CDC/metastability verification. Quartus/ModelSim remain the actual RTL verification tools.
mips-fifo-digital-design.alt: Explanatory MIPS datapath and separate eight by eight FIFO project boundaries
mips-fifo-digital-design.context: MIPS project · Oct–Dec 2023 | FIFO project · Feb–May 2024
mips-fifo-digital-design.credit: Original explanatory RTL diagram. The processor and FIFO are separate projects.

documented.title: Problem
paragraphs: I designed and emulated a 32-bit single-cycle MIPS processor in VHDL and implemented separate FIFO designs in Verilog. These projects explore instruction execution and ordered data storage through RTL and testbenches.

documented.title: Constraint
paragraphs: The processor needs a coherent instruction path through control, register access, the ALU, and memory. A FIFO must preserve ordering while making full and empty conditions explicit. These are different verification problems, so the two projects are described separately.

documented.title: Decision
paragraphs: For the processor, I used VHDL with Quartus Prime and ModelSim to design and validate the 32-bit single-cycle implementation. For the FIFO work, I implemented synchronous and asynchronous designs with 8 × 8 memory, boundary flags, and a testbench for storage and retrieval.

documented.title: Result
paragraphs: The MIPS project ran October–December 2023. The FIFO project ran February–May 2024 and included full / empty and almost-full / almost-empty status. My contribution covered RTL implementation and simulation-based validation.

connected-iot-systems.title: Connected IoT sensing & control
connected-iot-systems.focus: ESP8266/MQTT remote switching and a separate Arduino/ESP8266 crop-protection sensing prototype.
flow: User command
A web/mobile interface provides the requested output state in the documented switch project. Desired state and reported state are different facts.
Broker transport
MQTT connects the command publisher to the device. A broker connection does not prove the microcontroller received or applied the command.
Device firmware
ESP8266 firmware interprets a message and controls an output. The separate agriculture prototype adds PIR and ultrasonic sensing around Arduino Uno and ESP8266.
Acknowledgment
The teaching lab makes delivery delay, lost acknowledgments, reconnect behavior, and malformed payload rejection visible.
decisions: Desired vs reported state
A successful publish should not be confused with a confirmed physical output.
Track a command ID, pending state, device application, and acknowledgment.
Reconnect policy
A device returning after an outage needs a clear policy for the latest desired state.
Compare retained and non-retained commands in the model.
Input validation
A connected interface should not turn an arbitrary payload into an output change.
Reject malformed commands and keep the previous output unchanged.
try: Send ON, disconnect Wi-Fi, then send OFF with retained commands enabled.
Reconnect Wi-Fi and inspect desired state, device output, and acknowledgment.
Drop an ACK or send an invalid payload; use Query device to reconcile reported state.
connected-iot-systems.assumption: Local command/acknowledgment teaching model with synthetic latency. Retained commands represent the latest requested state. No mains switching, real device, or network connection is controlled.
connected-iot-systems.alt: Remote interface, MQTT path, ESP8266 or Arduino firmware, and a physical switch or sensor boundary
connected-iot-systems.credit: Original explanatory diagram based on the two resume projects.

documented.title: Problem
paragraphs: I built connected-device projects that translated remote commands and sensor inputs into microcontroller behavior: an ESP8266 / MQTT switching system and an Arduino-based crop-protection prototype.

documented.title: Constraint
paragraphs: A network command and a physical device action are separate events. Sensing also needs to distinguish the observed input from the action taken in response. Those boundaries matter when connectivity fails or a sensor changes state.

documented.title: Decision
paragraphs: For remote switching, I developed an IoT system supporting web and mobile control with ESP8266 and MQTT. For crop protection, I integrated PIR and ultrasonic sensors with Arduino Uno / ESP8266 hardware for intrusion monitoring.

documented.title: Result
paragraphs: The remote-switching project ran January–April 2021. The crop-protection prototype ran June–September 2020. I developed the connected control and sensing behavior across the microcontroller and communication interfaces.

fuzzy-logic-forecasting.title: Python fuzzy-logic forecasting
fuzzy-logic-forecasting.focus: A documented Python fuzzy-logic electricity-price forecasting role, with statistical analysis and refinement of membership functions and defuzzification.
fuzzy-logic-forecasting.context: Config Software Solution · Firmware Developer · Jan – Aug 2022
fuzzy-logic-forecasting.alt: Fuzzy inference pipeline: inputs, membership functions, rule evaluation, and an illustrative output index

documented.title: Problem
paragraphs: At Config Software Solution, I developed a Python fuzzy-logic system for electricity-price forecasting. My role ran January–August 2022.

documented.title: Constraint
paragraphs: A fuzzy forecast depends on the input domain, membership functions, inference rules, and the method used to combine outputs. A number is useful only when the model behavior can be evaluated against data.

documented.title: Decision
paragraphs: I used statistical analysis to evaluate performance and refine membership functions and defuzzification methods. The work joined Python implementation with inspection of how model settings affected behavior.

documented.title: Result
paragraphs: I contributed the Python fuzzy-logic forecasting system and its analytical refinement. This is my documented applied-AI work; my current use of Claude and coding agents is for coding and debugging.

flow: Normalized inputs
Demand, renewable availability, and trend are illustrative input variables for this browser model.
Membership functions
Low, medium, and high memberships overlap. Each input can partially activate more than one rule.
Rule evaluation
Rule strengths combine memberships and weight a small set of explicit output values.
Output & inspection
A weighted output index, memberships, and rule contributions make the reasoning visible.
decisions: Interpretability
A numeric result should be traceable to the rules that contributed to it.
Inspect every activation strength and weighted contribution.
Input scale
Membership functions assume a defined input domain.
Normalize and bound inputs before comparing rule behavior.
Evaluation
A smooth demonstration is not evidence of forecast accuracy.
Use a held-out dataset and suitable error metrics when evaluating a real forecasting model.
try: Raise demand while reducing renewable availability. Inspect which rules activate.
Move near a membership boundary and see overlapping rules blend the output.
Change trend and compare the relative index; export rule contributions.
fuzzy-logic-forecasting.assumption: New zero-order weighted-rule teaching example, not the original Python forecasting implementation. Output is a relative index, not a market price, investment signal, or validated prediction.
